title: Pulling stars, issues, and pull requests
text: Every call routed gh::gh(), reads personal access token GITHUB_PAT environment variable. Without token held 60 requests per hour, enough non-trivial account; fine-grained PAT (read-Metadata, Contents, Issues) limit 5,000 requests per hour. /search/issues endpoint used include = c("issues", "prs") per-query ceiling 1,000 results.
code: # In your .Renviron or a session: # GITHUB_PAT=ghp_xxx Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT") != ""

title: Pulling stars, issues, and pull requests
text: Calling function include argument preserves original behavior: single tibble commits, derived date, hour, weekday, year columns ready plotting helpers.
code: library(ghreadme)  commits <- collect_git_commits(   user   = "your-username",   emails = c("you@example.com", "you@work.example.com") )  head(commits)

title: Pulling stars, issues, and pull requests
text: include = "stars" returns one row per non-fork repo , star, fork, watcher counts plus language description. Rows sorted descending order stars. common use “top-starred repos” bar chart README:
code: stats <- collect_git_commits(   user    = "your-username",   include = "stars" ) stats$stars library(ggplot2)  stats$stars |>   head(10) |>   ggplot(aes(     x = stargazers_count,     y = reorder(repo, stargazers_count)   )) +   geom_col(fill = "#1E5F8C") +   labs(     x = "Stars",     y = NULL,     title = "Top 10 repos by stars"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Pulling stars, issues, and pull requests
text: include = "issues" hits /search/issues endpoint author:<user> type:issue, returns issues anywhere GitHub opened (just repos). row carries repo (owner/name), number, title, state, created_at, closed_at, issue url. small “issues opened per year, state” summary:
code: stats <- collect_git_commits(   user    = "your-username",   include = "issues" ) stats$issues library(dplyr)  stats$issues |>   mutate(year = as.integer(format(created_at, "%Y"))) |>   count(year, state) |>   tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = state, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

title: Pulling stars, issues, and pull requests
text: include = "prs" shares schema issues filters search type:pr. state field (open closed) applies. “merge rate” approximation, treating closed PRs merged (search endpoint distinguish merged closed-without-merging; pull detail endpoint per PR need ):
code: stats <- collect_git_commits(   user    = "your-username",   include = "prs" ) stats$prs stats$prs |>   count(state) |>   mutate(pct = n / sum(n))

title: Pulling stars, issues, and pull requests
text: Passing multiple values include switches return type single tibble named list, one element per requested type. one-shot “profile stats” summary suitable top profile README:
code: stats <- collect_git_commits(   user    = "your-username",   emails  = "you@example.com",   include = c("commits", "stars", "issues", "prs") )  names(stats) #> [1] "commits" "stars" "issues" "prs" tibble::tibble(   metric = c("Public repos", "Total stars", "Commits", "Issues opened",              "Pull requests opened"),   value  = c(     nrow(stats$stars),     sum(stats$stars$stargazers_count),     nrow(stats$commits),     nrow(stats$issues),     nrow(stats$prs)   ) ) |>   knitr::kable()

title: Animating Git visualizations with gifski
text: recipes also assume data-collection ggplot-based plot helpers ghreadme: Calling collect_git_commits() include argument returns original commits-tibble shape, exactly plot functions expect. also want star counts, authored issues, authored pull requests call, see vignette("gh-stats"); multi-include path returns named list, case recipes use stats$commits place bare commits object.

title: Animating Git visualizations with gifski
text: recipe follows pattern: Create temporary directory PNG frames. Loop, building one ggplot per frame writing ggsave(). Call make_gif() assemble frames GIF. make_gif() exported ghreadme handles collecting PNGs, building per-frame delay vector, calling gifski::gifski(). first_duration last_duration arguments let hold opening closing frames longer readers time register start end states. three recipes follow pattern differ plotted frame.

what: Recipe 1: cumulative commits, sliding the end date
title: Animating Git visualizations with gifski
text: cumulative_line_plot() already shows growth time, stepping date_end forward one month time makes growth feel kinetic — lines appear, lengthen, overtake one another repos accumulate commits. Note: Start date_seq one month date_begin. date_end equals date_begin first iteration commits exist exact day, cumulative_line_plot() error “commits filtering.”
code: date_seq <- seq(   from = as.Date("2023-02-01"),  # one month after date_begin   to   = max(commits$date),   by   = "1 month" )  cum_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "cumulative-frames") dir.create(cum_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)  for (i in seq_along(date_seq)) {   p <- cumulative_line_plot(     commits,     date_begin = "2023-01-01",     date_end   = date_seq[[i]],     top_n      = 8   )   ggsave(     filename = file.path(cum_dir, sprintf("%04d.png", i)),     plot     = p,     width = 1000, height = 600, units = "px", dpi = 96, bg = "white"   ) }  make_gif(cum_dir, "cumulative.gif",          width = 1000, height = 600,          first_duration = 1, frame_duration = 0.4, last_duration = 4)

what: Recipe 2: calendar heatmap, year by year
title: Animating Git visualizations with gifski
text: calendar_heatmap_plot() strong fit slow reveal: frame adds one year history, GIF builds toward present. plot’s date_begin argument honoured filtering, need bump date_end end next year.
code: years <- sort(unique(commits$year))  cal_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "calendar-frames") dir.create(cal_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)  for (i in seq_along(years)) {   p <- calendar_heatmap_plot(     commits,     date_begin = paste0(min(years), "-01-01"),     date_end   = paste0(years[[i]], "-12-31"),     title      = paste("Through", years[[i]])   )   ggsave(     filename = file.path(cal_dir, sprintf("%04d.png", i)),     plot     = p,     width = 1100, height = 700, units = "px", dpi = 96, bg = "white"   ) }  make_gif(cal_dir, "calendar.gif",          width = 1100, height = 700,          first_duration = 1, frame_duration = 1.2, last_duration = 4)

title: Animating Git visualizations with gifski
text: third pattern cycles repositories instead time — punchcard_plot() rendered per repo, GIF feels like flipping deck cards. example ranks repos commit count; see “Rank stars” tip API-backed alternative.
code: top_repos <- commits |>   dplyr::count(repo, sort = TRUE) |>   dplyr::slice_head(n = 6) |>   dplyr::pull(repo)  punch_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "punchcard-frames") dir.create(punch_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)  for (i in seq_along(top_repos)) {   p <- punchcard_plot(commits, repo = top_repos[[i]], title = top_repos[[i]])   ggsave(     filename = file.path(punch_dir, sprintf("%04d.png", i)),     plot     = p,     width = 1000, height = 500, units = "px", dpi = 96, bg = "white"   ) }  make_gif(punch_dir, "punchcard.gif",          width = 1000, height = 500,          first_duration = 1, frame_duration = 1.5, last_duration = 4)

title: Animating Git visualizations with gifski
text: Frame count vs file size. GIFs uncompressed across frames, monthly cadence five years (60 frames) renders nicely; daily cadence produces multi-megabyte file. Pick step yields 20–80 frames. Final-frame hold. last_duration (seconds) gives readers time absorb end state GIF loops. 3–5 seconds good range. Consistent axes. plots auto-scale per frame, makes axes jitter data added. bothers , pass explicit date_begin /date_end x-axis stays fixed across frames. Spiral plots. spiral_points_plot(), spiral_heatmap_plot(), spiral_horizon_plot() draw grid/spiralize graphics system rather returning ggplot objects. already compatible ggsave() + gifski::gifski() approach used — save frame grDevices::png() / dev.() pass resulting file list directly gifski::gifski(). Rank stars. punchcard recipe ranks repos commit count. rank GitHub stars instead, ask collect_git_commits() types pull carousel order stars element:
code: stats <- collect_git_commits(   user    = "your-username",   emails  = "you@example.com",   include = c("commits", "stars") ) top_repos <- head(stats$stars$repo, 6) # then iterate with punchcard_plot(stats$commits, repo = top_repos[[i]], ...)
